_meta.schema: exact: token -> {year, summary, good_for, notes, source}; alias: token -> canonical exact token it reuses (same schedule, different spelling). Lookup order: exact, then alias, then prefix. Year is approximate (paper / ComfyUI integration) and null when it could not be established from the registering pack's source.
_meta.source_field: Optional `source` records HOW the fact is known: kind ∈ vendor-default | vendor-doc | pack-provided | community | empirical | paper. Model recipes live in models.json, cited to the shipped template they came from. See .claude/rules/corpus-ground-truth.md.
_meta.behavioural_claims: Any statement about WHERE a schedule spends its steps is measured, never remembered — `just corpus-check` computes the real sigma curve and prints the step allocation across noise bands beside every entry that makes such a claim. Two entries here (beta57, linear_quadratic) previously described the opposite of what they do.

simple.summary: Naive equally-spaced sigma schedule. The plainest scheduler — used with samplers that bring their own pacing, and the reference schedule for recent rectified-flow models.
simple.good_for: The standard pick on recent rectified-flow models — euler + simple is what ComfyUI's own templates ship for most of the FLUX / Krea / Qwen-Image / Wan family. Also useful when a sampler brings its own pacing (dpm_adaptive, dpm_fast). On eps/v-prediction models (SD1.5, SDXL) karras or sgm_uniform usually beat it
simple.notes: Per-model step counts and CFG values live in models.json, cited to the template they came from, so they are stated once and re-verified against upstream rather than copied into prose here.

normal.summary: Standard scheduler matching the model's training noise schedule. Conservative default.
normal.good_for: Safe starting point that matches the model's training, whatever the architecture; a fine first pick before trying karras or sgm_uniform on eps/v-prediction models, and a common alternative to simple with euler on the FLUX family

karras.summary: Karras EDM noise schedule (Karras et al, 'Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models'). The most popular general-purpose schedule for eps/v-prediction models (SD1.5, SDXL).
karras.good_for: Default workhorse for dpmpp_2m, dpmpp_2m_sde, euler, heun on SD1.5/SDXL; still a good pairing with dpmpp_2m on recent rectified-flow models such as Qwen-Image. Those newer models more often want simple, normal or beta

exponential.summary: Exponential sigma spacing. Smoother transition between high and low noise than karras.
exponential.good_for: Alternative to karras when results look harsh; especially good with dpmpp_2m_sde

sgm_uniform.summary: SGM-style uniform spacing in noise level. The SDXL native schedule.
sgm_uniform.good_for: SDXL canonical pairing; required by some distilled models (Turbo, LCM)

ddim_uniform.summary: Uniform spacing in DDIM's parameterization. Pairs with the ddim sampler.
ddim_uniform.good_for: Pair with ddim sampler; SDXL refiner workflows

beta.summary: Beta-distribution spaced schedule. Concentrates steps where the model needs them most.
beta.good_for: A common pick on recent rectified-flow models such as the FLUX family (with euler, dpmpp_2m or ipndm); on SD1.5/SDXL, reach for it when karras/exponential look off

linear_quadratic.summary: Linear-then-quadratic spacing, from the flow-matching video models. Heavily weighted toward the HIGH-noise end: the linear half of the steps sit within ~2.5% of maximum sigma, so most of the budget goes to composition, and the low-noise detail end is crossed in a handful of large jumps.
linear_quadratic.good_for: Video diffusion (LTX-Video and similar), its original home. Also reported to work well on images with the ancestral CFG++ samplers (euler_ancestral_cfg_pp) — an ancestral sampler keeps injecting noise, and dwelling at high sigma lets it keep reshaping composition. Expect exploration, not refinement
linear_quadratic.notes: Measured, not assumed: at 20 steps the first 11 sigmas are all above 14.0 of a 14.6 maximum. This entry previously claimed the opposite ("heavily weighted toward the low-noise end") — the source builds sub-2.5% values and then inverts them with `1.0 - x`, and the inversion was missed. Re-check with `just corpus-check`.

kl_optimal.summary: KL-divergence-optimal schedule. Theoretically optimal noise placement under a KL objective.

bong_tangent.summary: RES4LYF custom schedule using a tangent-based pacing curve. Tuned for the RES4LYF RK sampler family.
bong_tangent.good_for: Pair with RES4LYF samplers (res_Ns, rk_*, lawson_*, etc.); also a well-liked pairing with dpmpp_2m on the FLUX family
bong_tangent.notes: Ships with the RES4LYF custom-node pack, not ComfyUI core — it only appears in the scheduler list when that pack is installed.

beta57.summary: The beta schedule at alpha=0.5 / beta=0.7 (core's beta defaults to 0.6/0.6). Beta-distribution sigma spacing: relative to the uniform simple schedule it takes steps out of the mid-noise range and spends them at the low-noise end, where fine detail is resolved.
beta57.good_for: Recent rectified-flow models such as FLUX and Qwen-Image; strong with euler, dpmpp_2m and ipndm. Also reported to pair well with the ancestral CFG++ samplers (euler_ancestral_cfg_pp) — the extra low-noise steps give an ancestral sampler's per-step noise injection room to resolve into detail
beta57.notes: Ships with the RES4LYF custom-node pack, not ComfyUI core — RES4LYF registers it as `beta_scheduler(alpha=0.5, beta=0.7)` against core's 0.6/0.6 defaults, so it is absent from core's SCHEDULER_HANDLERS and only appears when that pack is installed. The low-noise weighting is measured: at 20 steps it puts 11 steps below 10% of maximum sigma against simple's 9, taking them out of the mid-noise range.

unipc.summary: WanVideoWrapper's default flow-matching scheduler. Couples UniPC integration with Wan's sigma trajectory — picks both the algorithm and the schedule in one widget.
unipc.good_for: Wan2.x I2V/T2V; usually the first scheduler to try on a fresh Wan workflow

unipc/beta.summary: WanVideoWrapper's unipc with beta-distribution sigma spacing. Concentrates steps where the model needs them most.
unipc/beta.good_for: Wan2.x when unipc's stock pacing looks off — beta spacing can help detail in late steps

dpm++.summary: WanVideoWrapper's DPM-Solver++ adaptation for flow matching. Deterministic multistep.
dpm++.good_for: Wan2.x when you want DPM++ character; some users find it cleaner than unipc on still-heavy clips

dpm++/beta.summary: WanVideoWrapper's dpm++ with beta-distribution sigma spacing.

dpm++_sde.summary: WanVideoWrapper's DPM-Solver++ in SDE form — adds noise each step. Stochastic variant of dpm++.
dpm++_sde.good_for: Wan2.x when motion-heavy clips look stale; SDE can add variety

dpm++_sde/beta.summary: WanVideoWrapper's dpm++_sde with beta-distribution sigma spacing.

euler.summary: WanVideoWrapper's Euler adaptation for flow matching. Backed by Diffusers' FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler. The simplest predictable baseline.
euler.good_for: Wan2.x conservative baseline; useful as a reference when comparing other schedulers

euler/beta.summary: WanVideoWrapper's flow-matching Euler with beta-distribution sigma spacing.

longcat_distill_euler.summary: WanVideoWrapper's Euler tuned for LongCat-distilled Wan checkpoints. Applies a fixed 50-step distillation pacing curve regardless of the steps widget.
longcat_distill_euler.good_for: LongCat-distilled Wan checkpoints; likely off-target outside that lineage
longcat_distill_euler.notes: Specialized for LongCat distillation — pacing is fixed by the distillation, not the steps widget

deis.summary: WanVideoWrapper's DEIS (Diffusion Exponential Integrator) for flow matching. Multistep.
deis.good_for: Wan2.x few-step regimes (8-15); some users like DEIS for clean motion

lcm.summary: WanVideoWrapper's Latent Consistency scheduler for flow matching. Designed for LCM-distilled Wan checkpoints.
lcm.good_for: LCM-distilled Wan checkpoints only; off-target on non-distilled weights

lcm/beta.summary: WanVideoWrapper's lcm with beta-distribution sigma spacing.

res_multistep.summary: WanVideoWrapper's RES (Hochbruck-Ostermann exponential RK) multistep scheduler for flow matching.
res_multistep.good_for: Wan2.x alternative to dpm++; some users find RES handles fine detail well

er_sde.summary: WanVideoWrapper's ER-SDE (Exponential-Reverse SDE) scheduler for flow matching.
er_sde.good_for: Wan2.x experimental SDE alternative; worth a try when default schedulers feel stale

flowmatch_causvid.summary: WanVideoWrapper scheduler tuned for CausVid (causal video) distilled checkpoints.
flowmatch_causvid.good_for: CausVid-distilled Wan workflows; behavior outside that context is model-dependent

flowmatch_distill.summary: WanVideoWrapper scheduler for generic flow-matching distilled checkpoints — fewer-step pacing curve.
flowmatch_distill.good_for: Distilled Wan checkpoints aiming for low step counts (4-12)

flowmatch_pusa.summary: WanVideoWrapper scheduler tuned for Pusa-style flow-matching variants.
flowmatch_pusa.good_for: Pusa-style Wan checkpoints; behavior outside that context is model-dependent

multitalk.summary: WanVideoWrapper scheduler tuned for the MultiTalk lip-sync / audio-driven workflows.
multitalk.good_for: MultiTalk audio-driven Wan workflows; off-target otherwise

sa_ode_stable.summary: WanVideoWrapper's stabilized SA-ODE (Stochastic Adams ODE) scheduler for flow matching.
sa_ode_stable.good_for: Wan2.x experimental; SA-Solver family is known for solid few-step performance

rcm.summary: WanVideoWrapper's rCM (reverse Consistency Model) flow-matching scheduler.

vibt_unipc.summary: WanVideoWrapper's ViBT UniPC variant — newer addition with adjusted tangent treatment.
vibt_unipc.good_for: Wan2.x when standard unipc results look stale; less battle-tested than unipc

FlowMatchDiscreteScheduler.summary: HunyuanVideoWrapper's default scheduler. Discrete-time flow-matching Euler — the simplest, most predictable choice.
FlowMatchDiscreteScheduler.good_for: HunyuanVideo default; usually the first to try on a fresh HunyuanVideo workflow

DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.summary: HunyuanVideoWrapper using Diffusers' DPM-Solver++ multistep, deterministic mode.
DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.good_for: HunyuanVideo when you want DPM++ character; some users prefer it over FlowMatchDiscrete on detail-heavy clips

SDE-DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.summary: HunyuanVideoWrapper using Diffusers' DPM-Solver++ multistep in SDE form — adds noise each step.
SDE-DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.good_for: HunyuanVideo when motion-heavy clips look stale; SDE adds variety at some cost in determinism

SASolverScheduler.good_for: HunyuanVideo few-step regimes; SA-Solver family is competitive at 10-20 steps

UniPCMultistepScheduler.summary: HunyuanVideoWrapper using Diffusers' UniPC multistep predictor-corrector.
UniPCMultistepScheduler.good_for: HunyuanVideo at lower step counts (10-20) when you want UniPC convergence behavior

Default for model.summary: HiDream-Sampler passthrough — uses whichever scheduler the loaded model recommends. The least surprising option when you're unsure.
Default for model.good_for: HiDream when you want the checkpoint's recommended pacing without thinking about it

UniPC.summary: HiDream-Sampler's UniPC option (display-name). Standard UniPC predictor-corrector. Maps to the same algorithm as core uni_pc.
UniPC.good_for: HiDream at low step counts (10-15) for predictor-corrector convergence

Euler.summary: HiDream-Sampler's Euler option (display-name). Plain first-order Euler — the simplest baseline.
Euler.good_for: HiDream conservative baseline; predictable and fast

Karras Euler.summary: HiDream-Sampler's Euler with Karras sigma spacing.
Karras Euler.good_for: HiDream when Euler results need better noise pacing — Karras spacing usually helps with detail

Karras Exponential.summary: HiDream-Sampler's Karras exponential schedule. Smoother sigma transitions than Karras Euler's underlying schedule.
Karras Exponential.good_for: HiDream when Karras Euler looks harsh; exponential pacing tends to be gentler

AYS SD1.summary: Impact/Inspire label for core ComfyUI's AlignYourStepsScheduler with model_type SD1. Not a schedule of the pack's own — the label is parsed and the core node does the work.
AYS SD1.good_for: SD 1.5 checkpoints inside the detailer/iterative nodes, which cannot reach the core AlignYourStepsScheduler node directly
AYS SD1.notes: comfyui-impact-pack modules/impact/impact_sampling.py, calculate_sigmas(): a scheduler starting with 'AYS' calls AlignYourStepsScheduler().get_sigmas(scheduler[4:], steps, denoise=1.0), so the text after 'AYS ' is passed straight through as model_type. Core offers exactly SD1, SDXL and SVD.

AYS SDXL.summary: Impact/Inspire label for core ComfyUI's AlignYourStepsScheduler with model_type SDXL. Same dispatch as AYS SD1, different model_type.
AYS SDXL.good_for: SDXL checkpoints inside the detailer/iterative nodes
AYS SDXL.notes: Same call site as AYS SD1 — comfyui-impact-pack modules/impact/impact_sampling.py, calculate_sigmas().

AYS SVD.summary: Impact/Inspire label for core ComfyUI's AlignYourStepsScheduler with model_type SVD. Same dispatch as AYS SD1, different model_type.
AYS SVD.good_for: Stable Video Diffusion checkpoints inside the detailer/iterative nodes
AYS SVD.notes: Same call site as AYS SD1 — comfyui-impact-pack modules/impact/impact_sampling.py, calculate_sigmas().

GITS[coeff=1.2].summary: Impact/Inspire label for core ComfyUI's GITSScheduler. The number inside the brackets is not decoration — it is parsed out of the label and passed as the coeff argument, and 1.2 is the core node's own default.
GITS[coeff=1.2].good_for: Reaching GITS from the detailer/iterative nodes, which take a scheduler name rather than a SIGMAS input
GITS[coeff=1.2].notes: comfyui-impact-pack modules/impact/impact_sampling.py: a scheduler starting with 'GITS[coeff=' calls GITSScheduler().execute(float(scheduler[11:-1]), steps, denoise=1.0). Only the coeff=1.2 label is offered (modules/impact/core.py, ADDITIONAL_SCHEDULERS), so this is the one point on a knob core exposes over 0.80-1.50.

LTXV[default].summary: Impact/Inspire label for core ComfyUI's LTXVScheduler, called with every argument hard-coded. Worth knowing before you pick it: the step count is fixed at 20 in the call, so the node's own steps widget does not reach this schedule.
LTXV[default].good_for: LTX-Video work inside the detailer/iterative nodes, at the vendor's default shift settings and nowhere else — anything else needs the core LTXVScheduler node
LTXV[default].notes: comfyui-impact-pack modules/impact/impact_sampling.py calls LTXVScheduler().execute(20, 2.05, 0.95, True, 0.1) — steps=20, max_shift=2.05, base_shift=0.95, stretch=True, terminal=0.1. The last four are the core node's declared defaults (comfy_extras/nodes_lt.py); steps=20 is also its default, but here it is a constant rather than a passthrough.

OSS FLUX.summary: Impact/Inspire label for core ComfyUI's OptimalStepsScheduler with model_type FLUX. Same label-parsing trick as the AYS entries.
OSS FLUX.good_for: FLUX checkpoints inside the detailer/iterative nodes
OSS FLUX.notes: comfyui-impact-pack modules/impact/impact_sampling.py: a scheduler starting with 'OSS' calls OptimalStepsScheduler().execute(scheduler[4:], steps, denoise=1.0). Core offers exactly FLUX, Wan and Chroma (comfy_extras/nodes_optimalsteps.py).

OSS Wan.summary: Impact/Inspire label for core ComfyUI's OptimalStepsScheduler with model_type Wan.
OSS Wan.good_for: Wan checkpoints inside the detailer/iterative nodes
OSS Wan.notes: Same call site as OSS FLUX — comfyui-impact-pack modules/impact/impact_sampling.py.

OSS Chroma.summary: Impact/Inspire label for core ComfyUI's OptimalStepsScheduler with model_type Chroma.
OSS Chroma.good_for: Chroma checkpoints inside the detailer/iterative nodes
OSS Chroma.notes: Same call site as OSS FLUX — comfyui-impact-pack modules/impact/impact_sampling.py.

align_your_steps.summary: comfyui-easy-use's AlignYourSteps entry. Unlike the Impact labels it picks the model type for you: it reads the loaded checkpoint's version and passes SD1 / SDXL / SVD accordingly, falling back to SDXL when the version cannot be determined.
align_your_steps.good_for: AYS on the easy preSampling* nodes without having to name the architecture yourself; the auto-detection is the reason to prefer it over a fixed AYS label
align_your_steps.notes: comfyui-easy-use py/nodes/samplers.py: get_sd_version(model), then alignYourStepsScheduler().get_sigmas(model_type.upper(), steps, denoise), with model_type defaulted to 'sdxl' when it comes back 'unknown'. py/nodes/fix.py maps the same token onto the Impact-style 'AYS SDXL' / 'AYS SVD' / 'AYS SD1' labels for the detailer path.

gits.summary: comfyui-easy-use's GITS entry. Routes to the same GITS sigma table core ships, at coeff 1.2 — the coeff comes from the node's custom settings and defaults to 1.2.
gits.good_for: GITS on the easy preSampling* nodes without wiring a SIGMAS input
gits.notes: comfyui-easy-use py/nodes/samplers.py: gitsScheduler().get_sigmas(coeff, steps, denoise) with coeff read from loader_settings['custom'] and defaulted to 1.2; the plain (non-custom) path calls it with coeff=1.2 literally.

karrasADV.summary: comfyui-easy-use's karras entry with the knobs exposed. It calls core's KarrasScheduler node rather than the plain karras handler, so sigma_max, sigma_min and rho are yours to set — defaults 14.61, 0.03 and 7.0. Same schedule as karras when you leave them alone.
karrasADV.good_for: When plain karras is right but its endpoints are not — clipping sigma_max or moving rho is the whole point of the ADV form
karrasADV.notes: comfyui-easy-use py/nodes/samplers.py, get_sampler_custom(): KarrasScheduler.execute(steps, sigma_max, sigma_min, rho) with those three read from loader_settings['custom']. Only the easy preSamplingCustom node offers it.

exponentialADV.summary: comfyui-easy-use's exponential entry with the endpoints exposed. Calls core's ExponentialScheduler node, so sigma_max and sigma_min are yours to set (defaults 14.61 and 0.03). Same schedule as exponential otherwise.
exponentialADV.good_for: Exponential spacing over a hand-chosen sigma range rather than the model's own
exponentialADV.notes: comfyui-easy-use py/nodes/samplers.py: ExponentialScheduler.execute(steps, sigma_max, sigma_min). Only the easy preSamplingCustom node offers it.

polyExponential.summary: comfyui-easy-use's entry for core's PolyexponentialScheduler — polynomial-in-log-sigma spacing, with sigma_max, sigma_min and rho exposed (defaults 14.61, 0.03, 7.0).
polyExponential.good_for: A third spacing curve to try alongside karrasADV and exponentialADV when none of the plain schedules suit
polyExponential.notes: comfyui-easy-use py/nodes/samplers.py: PolyexponentialScheduler.execute(steps, sigma_max, sigma_min, rho). Only the easy preSamplingCustom node offers it.

sdturbo.summary: comfyui-easy-use's entry for core's SDTurboScheduler — the very short schedule SD-Turbo checkpoints were distilled for. It reads the schedule off the model, so it takes model, steps and denoise rather than sigma endpoints.
sdturbo.good_for: SD-Turbo and similarly distilled checkpoints at 1-4 steps; off-target on undistilled weights
sdturbo.notes: comfyui-easy-use py/nodes/samplers.py: SDTurboScheduler.execute(model, steps, denoise). Only the easy preSamplingCustom node offers it.

vp.summary: comfyui-easy-use's entry for core's VPScheduler — the variance-preserving schedule from the score-SDE formulation. Parameterised by beta_d, beta_min and eps_s (all defaulting to 0.1 here) rather than by sigma endpoints.
vp.good_for: Matching a variance-preserving training schedule; the three betas are the knobs, and the defaults are easy-use's own rather than a model's
vp.notes: comfyui-easy-use py/nodes/samplers.py: VPScheduler.execute(steps, beta_d, beta_min, eps_s), each read from loader_settings['custom'] and defaulted to 0.1. Only the easy preSamplingCustom node offers it.

constant.summary: Not a sigma schedule. On RES4LYF's ClownScheduler this widget shapes a weight curve, and 'constant' is the opt-out: hold the value flat instead of ramping it along any curve. It is prepended to the scheduler list, not part of it.
constant.good_for: Turning a ClownScheduler ramp off — a flat guide/weight value between its start and end steps. Choosing it expecting a noise schedule will not do what you want
constant.notes: RES4LYF sigmas.py, ClownScheduler.INPUT_TYPES: "scheduler": (["constant"] + get_res4lyf_scheduler_list(), ...). The guide code branches on it explicitly (beta/rk_guide_func_beta.py is full of `if scheduler_ != "constant":`), which is what makes it a sentinel rather than a curve. Also offered by Legacy_ClownsharKSamplerGuides.
